PullRequest.Title: chat: Run marketplace prompts in new sessions
PullRequest.Body: ## Screenshot and Video https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe97c83c-5847-4ad2-a9ba-fdbe00d13fb3 ## Summary - make customization marketplace “Try this” prompts install their item before launching - render prompts as compact, themed actions with the chat send icon - open the prompt in a new Copilot session in both the workbench and Agents Window - explicitly start those sessions without a selected workspace or working folder - preserve the no-workspace selection when Agent Host draft sessions are materialized ## Testing - `npm run compile` — passed - `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHostNewSessionFolderService.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\test\browser\sessionsActions.test.ts` — 131 passing - targeted ESLint for changed TypeScript files — passed - `git diff --check` — passed - launched the full authenticated Agents Window build and confirmed it reached CDP readiness

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Each representative query owns a separate enabled Button and callback; the install service explicitly coalesces only the install/repair promise, after which every waiter calls runPrompt. The sidebar command creates a UUID-backed resource per invocation and the Agent Host path directly calls connection.createSession without a cross-resource limiter. The exact number of users who multi-click is uncertain, but the fan-out mechanism and critical path are explicit.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Agent Host backend sessions, createSession IPC calls, and subsequent chat requests
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The burst grows with the number of distinct representative-query buttons clicked while one slow install or repair is pending; marketplace input validation permits up to 32 representative queries for an item.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Concurrent backend session startup and request dispatch can spike IPC/CPU/network work, contend with the foreground launch, and increase latency or reduce throughput.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Representative queries were inert list text, so opening an item or installing it could not queue multiple Agent Host session launches from this section.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every query is now an independent action. During an installation, additional query actions observe `installing`/`repairing` and join the same coalesced operation; when it settles, all handlers continue concurrently into `runPrompt`.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added handler disables only its own `button` at line 308. Other newly added query buttons remain enabled and independently await `ensureInstalled(resource)` before each invokes `this.options.runPrompt(query)`.
Findings.Title: Disable all query actions while a prompt launch is in flight
Findings.Impact: On a slow first install or repair, a user can click several still-enabled “Try this” prompts. Completion releases all waiters at once, opening and starting several Copilot sessions concurrently instead of one, causing a visible resource/latency spike.
Findings.Evidence: `renderQueries` creates one Button and async listener per query but disables only the clicked Button. `CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService.install`/`repair` returns the existing pending promise for the same resource, so all listeners resume together. `runMarketplacePrompt` invokes `openNewSessionSidebar.agent-host-copilotcli`; `openChatSession` generates a fresh UUID resource for every invocation and sends the prompt, while `AgentHostSessionHandler._createAndSubscribe` calls `connection.createSession`. The only observed sequencer is keyed by session resource, so distinct UUIDs are not globally limited.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a shared per-detail/per-resource launch-in-flight state: disable every query action when any query starts and re-enable them after that launch finishes (or serialize launches through one shared queue if multiple queued prompts are intentional). Keep the install service’s existing per-resource coalescing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a customization marketplace item and render its “Try this” prompts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The already-loaded marketplace resource is rendered synchronously into the detail pane; creating the query DOM and Button objects is on the detail-opening UI path, while README fetching remains separate existing work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Button/listener/icon allocation per representative query. Agent Finder validates at most 32 queries per item; normal fixtures contain zero or one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering is synchronous and single-threaded; rerenders dispose prior Buttons and clear the query DOM before rebuilding.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is involved. The resource is already available when setInput runs, and install-state changes rerender only install state rather than rebuilding queries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that work is O(query count) and bounded for the REST source; no evidence of a user-visible rendering regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Button construction is heavier than the former text nodes, but the validated cardinality is bounded and no layout read/write loop or expensive boundary is added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the extra synchronous UI work is bounded and small.

Scenarios.Scenario: Click one or more representative prompts for an available, installing, missing, or installed item
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For a cold item, install/repair must finish before prompt launch; then opening a unique Copilot session and sending the prompt are on the critical path. For an installed item, session opening and send are immediately critical.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install or repair the selected marketplace customization and reconcile/verify its installation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One operation per resource after the install service's pending-operation coalescing, even when several query handlers wait on it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The representative-query list was inert; installation occurred only through the existing explicit install/repair action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold prompt launch blocks until installation/repair completes; warm installed launches skip this boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a fresh Agent Host session and send the selected chat prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unique UUID-backed session and request per clicked query; multiple distinct buttons can release concurrently after the shared installation completes, up to the number clicked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No session launch or chat request was reachable from representative-query text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session creation and request dispatch must occur before each click reports success and contend when released together.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of distinct query buttons clicked while a slow install/repair is pending; source validation permits up to 32 representative queries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Install and repair are coalesced per resource, but each Button has an independent continuation. No cross-resource/global launch limiter was found; unique session resources bypass the per-key provisional sequencer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Installed state is the warm path and skips installation. Pending installs and repairs are positively coalesced; after completion, each waiting click still starts its own uncached session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: independent enabled buttons, coalesced install waiters, unique session UUIDs, direct createSession calls, and lack of a global limiter are all traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical items may expose only a few prompts and most users click once, but slow installs make exploratory multi-clicking realistic; exact Agent Host startup cost varies by provider and SDK warmth.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported a medium concurrency-burst regression because all waiting query actions fan out into simultaneous heavyweight session launches.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run a marketplace prompt in the Agents Window and preserve the explicit no-workspace choice through materialization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: openQuickChat selects a no-workspace session and sendQuery starts the request; folder-marker lookups are O(1) and precede working-directory resolution/session creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/newSessionAction.ts sendPrompt and Agent Host session handling
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize the Agent Host session and dispatch the prompt from the new session view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session/request for a normal click; multiple independently active query buttons can produce one per click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The new-session action did not accept or send a marketplace prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The prompt cannot progress until the session view sends the query and backend session setup begins.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of prompt actions invoked; no-folder lookups themselves remain constant time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single action is sequential. Separate query actions are not coalesced by the UI, which is covered by the reported burst finding.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No session cache is reused because the feature intentionally opens a new session. Folder choices are retained only for live session resources and cleared by chat-session disposal events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the command and send path; no separate folder-service performance regression is established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Backend startup cost depends on whether the Agent Host/SDK is warm; the marker operations are negligible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the shared multi-action burst.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a no-workspace Copilot sidebar session and transfer the marker from untitled to materialized resource
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The no-folder marker is set before opening/loading the view, then copied to the real resource during first-send materialization; constant-time ResourceSet operations do not block an external boundary materially.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load/materialize the new Agent Host session and send its initial request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per prompt action, with install-side multi-click fan-out as described above.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Prompt launches did not explicitly create no-workspace markers on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The marker is read before createSession so no working directory is selected; session creation remains the expensive critical operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously live or not-yet-disposed session resources.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ResourceSet access is synchronous O(1); backend creation is per unique session and has no global limiter found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The marker behaves as per-session state rather than a cache. Both untitled and real-resource entries are removed by IChatService.onDidDisposeSession; folder changes also clear applicable folder selections.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for normal lifecycle cleanup and O(1) lookup; lower on rare partial-open failure ownership, so that edge was not reported.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A failure before chat-session ownership attaches can leave a tiny marker until window disposal, but the realistic retained volume and user-visible cost are insufficient for a separate performance finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: normal lifetime is bounded to live sessions and the added lookup/state transfer is cheap.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 20 changed files and traced marketplace detail rendering, install/repair coalescing, new-session command paths, Agent Host createSession IPC, prompt dispatch, and no-workspace marker lifecycle. Submitted one medium concurrency-burst finding; no other changed mechanism met the performance evidence threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
